To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acute exposure to the 9/11 World Trade Center attack (e.g., being injured or being in the dust cloud), is significantly associated with later heart and lung diseases, but not with diabetes.

1) acute exposures of injury, dust cloud, and dust cloud immersion on 9/ 11 were significantly associated with later heart and lung diseases, 2) acute exposures of dust cloud and dust cloud immersion were not significantly associated with diabetes, 3) the associations between the acute exposures of dust and injury and heart and lung disease were not significantly modified by age at exposure, and 4) there was no evidence for a threshold for acute exposure to dust cloud or dust cloud immersion for
acute injury and dust cloud exposure on 9/ 11 were associated with heart disease, asthma, and other lung diseases, but not with diabetes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of acute exposures on the development of chronic disease.
the health effects of acute and chronic exposures of dust and other toxicants that were released during the terrorist attacks of September 11, 20011 (9/11).
the effects of acute and chronic exposures to environmental hazards on the health of persons exposed to them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 9/11 terrorist attacks of September, 2001, resulted in significant acute and chronic disease outcomes for the survivors of the attacks.

the 9/11 attack on the World Trade Center in New York City exposed many thousands of people to acute and chronic hazardous materials that have been associated with significant health effects, including asthma, heart disease and diabetes.

the World Trade Center attack on September 11,2001, exposed thousands of people who sustained injury, were in the dust cloud, or both to hazardous materials, which resulted in reports of acute and chronic health consequences, including psychological illness such as post-trauma stress disorder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the acute exposures to injury and dust cloud on 9/111/2001 have significant associations with later health problems.
acute exposure to dust cloud and injury on 9/12/2001 is associated with increased risk of chronic diseases such as asthma and heart disease.
the 9/11 attack had a significant impact on the physical and mental health of those exposed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 9/11 attack was not only an event of great loss of life and destruction but also an event that has had a lasting impact on the health and well-being of many of the survivors.
the 9/11 exposures are still affecting people’s health, and that the effects are not only physical, but also psychological.
the health consequences of 9/111 may extend beyond the initial acute phase and may include chronic disease.
